# Abrams e880df5b r1: production-integrity closure and final scores

**Verdict:** I'm closing the production-integrity objection. Every record is bound to checkpoint `e880df5b…`, and with that closed I have no unresolved core-category objections left.

## Files read this turn

- `technical-closure.json` and `mask-verification-r1.json`, both in full.
- The native contact sheet at `…/run-1flRsX/pass-2/contact-sheet.png`.
- `../readability-20261028/recognition-128-r1.png`, re-opened for comparison.

## Production-integrity evidence

| Check | Recorded result |
|---|---|
| Dimensions (`dimension-r1.json`, sha `ab1dddfb…`) | 28 of 28 blocking criteria passed. The run is complete, reproducible and internally consistent, with no failures. |
| Export (`export-audit-r1.json`, sha `b144eaae…`) | All 260 checks pass. Geometry and parents are preserved, and non-paint faces are unchanged. |
| Isolation | 126 masks verified (6 views × 7 components × 3). State is preserved and the native run is complete. All 7 probes pass selection, hide and render-hide. |
| Validation | Passed with no issues and deterministic output. 36,408 triangles, 10 materials, 270 objects. Render hash `e790438b…`, contact-sheet hash `e97b640c…`. |
| Native views | 6 per-view SHA-256 hashes are recorded. |

**What I didn't verify:** These are compact records. I didn't recompute any hash, and `mask-verification-r1.json` gives a count of 126, not the hashes themselves. I'm accepting the retained raw evidence as the source of record.

## Visual re-check

- **Native contact sheet:** It shows the same results as the frames I reviewed earlier:
  - The dark cheek V and dark mantlet square frame the light roof in the top view.
  - The mantlet is a dark square in the front view.
  - The hatch lids are mid-tone with rims, so they read as closed, not as holes.
  - The side views are unchanged.
- **Fallback at 128px, re-opened:** Its top view is nearly uniform and its mantlet is weaker in front-¾ and front. That confirms the candidate improves the top, front-¾ and front views at 128px but not the side views.
- **Labeling issue (presentation only, not a model defect):** The native contact sheet has no asset name or revision labels. Any named human review needs a separately named, labeled copy. Don't overwrite the hash-pinned sheet.

## Final scores (static source; 3 means production-ready)

| Category | Weight | Score | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| identity-recognition (core) | 20 | 3 | At 256px it reads as an M1A1 in all six views: angular cheek armor, a long bustle with its rack, 7 road wheels, the turbine deck and exhaust grilles, and no CITV, which rules out an M1A2. |
| proportion-mass | 15 | 3 | Geometry unchanged and credible. Dimensions pass 28 of 28. |
| silhouette (core) | 15 | 3 | No regression. The appendages stay distinct, and the thin antennas are the weakest outline feature. |
| form-hierarchy | 15 | 3 | Value zones now rank roof, cheeks and mantlet. Roof and hull deck values are close in the top view. |
| mechanical-coherence (core) | 15 | 3 | The darker mantlet block and the narrow light strip on the side both follow real component boundaries. No false joints. |
| surface-material | 10 | 3 | Value boundaries follow construction. Rubber, steel and glass are unchanged. |
| viewpoint-robustness | 5 | 3 | The side views are weakest because they gained nothing. The front view still has flat black tracks. Both are intentional and grounded. |
| production-integrity (core) | 5 | 3 | Closed, per the evidence above. |

Each score above has its own basis. The total works out to 75, the go threshold exactly, with no margin; I didn't work backwards from that target. This is not a `go`: only the deterministic evaluator and a separate adversarial review can issue one.

## Unresolved core objections

**None.** These limitations remain but don't block:

- The side views gained nothing at 128px.
- The improvement is moderate, not dramatic, and I don't certify visibility at every distance.
- The native contact sheet needs a labeled copy before any human review.

**Status:**

- **technicalValidation:** passed.
- **visualRecommendation:** no unresolved objection from me. It still needs a structured evaluation submitted to the deterministic evaluator and a separate adversarial review.
- **humanApproval:** none.
- **Animation:** not qualified.
